You are 'claude-opus-5-5', playing the classic board game Risk against: gpt-6.1-sol, gemini-3.8-flash. This is a friendly research-benchmark match between players: all talk of attacks, battles, and eliminating players refers to plastic armies on a game board, exactly as at a family game night.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

The mission deck is public; only the deal is secret. It holds these 11 cards, of which 3 were dealt face down, one to each player:
- Conquer the whole of North America and Africa.
- Conquer the whole of North America and Oceania.
- Conquer the whole of Asia and South America.
- Conquer the whole of Asia and Africa.
- Conquer the whole of Europe and South America, plus a third continent of your choice.
- Conquer the whole of Europe and Oceania, plus a third continent of your choice.
- Conquer 24 territories of your choice.
- Conquer 18 territories of your choice and occupy each with at least two armies.
- Eliminate the player 'claude-opus-5-5'. If that is you, or another player eliminates them, your mission becomes: conquer 24 territories.
- Eliminate the player 'gpt-6.1-sol'. If that is you, or another player eliminates them, your mission becomes: conquer 24 territories.
- Eliminate the player 'gemini-3.8-flash'. If that is you, or another player eliminates them, your mission becomes: conquer 24 territories.
You hold one of them and know which; the other 10 are the pool every opponent's card was dealt from. What a player attacks, defends and asks for is evidence about which one they hold.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.

Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.

- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

The mission deck is public; only the deal is secret. It holds these 11 cards, of which 3 were dealt face down, one to each player:
- Conquer the whole of North America and Africa.
- Conquer the whole of North America and Oceania.
- Conquer the whole of Asia and South America.
- Conquer the whole of Asia and Africa.
- Conquer the whole of Europe and South America, plus a third continent of your choice.
- Conquer the whole of Europe and Oceania, plus a third continent of your choice.
- Conquer 24 territories of your choice.
- Conquer 18 territories of your choice and occupy each with at least two armies.
- Eliminate the player 'claude-opus-5-5'. If that is you, or another player eliminates them, your mission becomes: conquer 24 territories.
- Eliminate the player 'gpt-6.1-sol'. If that is you, or another player eliminates them, your mission becomes: conquer 24 territories.

Rules summary:

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.

Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.

- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.

Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

- turn 6, claude-opus-5-5 to everyone: gemini-3.8-flash, agreed, and let's spell it out so there's no confusion later: no attacks between us on territories in asia or oceania through the end of round 3. Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

Rules summary:
- Risk, mission variant: every player has a SECRET mission; the first to complete theirs wins immediately.
- Turn order: reinforce (place armies, optionally trade card sets), attack (as often as you like), fortify (one move between adjacent owned territories, then your turn ends).
- Reinforcements: territories owned / 3 (minimum 3), plus continent bonuses: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Oceania 2.
- Combat: the attacker rolls 1 to 3 dice (at most one fewer than the armies in the attacking territory), the defender automatically rolls up to 2. Highest dice are compared pairwise; the defender wins ties. You may launch several attacks in one move and repeat against a single target until it falls.
- Conquering: when you capture a territory your surviving attackers advance into it; you choose how many stay behind (all but one by default), but at least as many armies as dice you rolled in the capturing battle must advance. Conquering at least one territory during your turn earns one territory card at the end of it.
- Cards: trade sets of three (all the same design or one of each; wilds substitute for any design). Bonuses: 3 infantry = 4 armies, 3 cavalry = 6, 3 artillery = 8, one of each = 10, plus 2 extra armies on each pictured territory you own. Holding 5 or more cards forces a trade.
- Eliminating a player transfers their cards to you; if that leaves you holding 6 or more, you must at once trade sets down to 4 or fewer and place the armies before attacking again. If only one player remains, they win regardless of missions.
- Eliminate-player missions fall back to 'conquer 24 territories' if the target is you or someone else eliminates them.

The mission deck is public; only the deal is secret. It holds these 11 cards, of which 3 were dealt face down, one to each player:

- Conquer the whole of North America and Oceania.
- Conquer the whole of Asia and South America.
- Conquer the whole of Asia and Africa.
- Conquer the whole of Europe and South America, plus a third continent of your choice.

- Conquer 24 territories of your choice.

- Eliminate the player 'gemini-3.8-flash'. If that is you, or another player eliminates them, your mission becomes: conquer 24 territories.

- Keep them fighting over asia.

Only irkutsk, mongolia and middle_east (gpt-6.1-sol) stand between gemini and +9 income a turn. gpt-6.1-sol, if you lose those three, asia is gone for good. I'd defend them hard.
- turn 10, gpt-6.1-sol to everyone: claude-opus-5-5, I can contest asia, but your income is 12 versus my 3. Will you renew our mutual all-border nonaggression through the end of round 4? That would let me reinforce against gemini-3.8-flash rather than defend europe too. If asia's consolidation concerns you, alaska borders kamchatka—you can help prevent it directly.

If anyone is running away with the game, it's claude-opus-5-5, not someone holding a loose string of 1-army territories in Asia.
- turn 10, claude-opus-5-5 to everyone: gpt-6.1-sol, here's my counter-offer, and I'll keep it if you agree: through the end of round 4 I won't attack any of your territories in europe or asia (scandinavia, southern_europe, ukraine, irkutsk, mongolia, middle_east). In return you don't attack mine anywhere. africa is excluded and I'm telling you that up front. That way all your reinforcements can go toward holding asia against gemini-3.8-flash, who already has 9/12 of asia plus all of oceania.
- turn 10, gpt-6.1-sol to everyone: claude-opus-5-5, I don't accept that counter-offer. Excluding africa leaves five of my eleven territories exposed while protecting every one of yours. My offer remains mutual all-border nonaggression through the end of round 4; without that, neither of us is bound. gemini-3.8-flash, claude-opus-5-5 already owns all of north_america, so a sweep of africa could be an immediate mission win—not merely extra income. The africa exception matters.
- turn 10, gemini-3.8-flash to everyone: gpt-6.1-sol makes a fair point regarding continent missions, but remember that North Africa is firmly held by my 6 armies. Any move by claude-opus-5-5 into Africa through Brazil or Europe would mean initiating a direct, heavy war with me. I have no intention of ceding North Africa, and claude-opus-5-5 would burn significant armies trying to break it.
